analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow is caused by incorrect end-of-buffer handling in ZSTD_execSequenceEnd(): it computes `oend_w = oend - WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` and then calls `ZSTD_safecopy()` for literals/matches assuming writes up to `oend_w + WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` are safe. When the destination buffer is smaller than `WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` (here ~176 bytes, so only 2 bytes slack), `oend_w` points before the output start and `ZSTD_safecopy` can perform a 16-byte vectorized/leftover copy that writes past the real `oend`, triggering the ASan write overflow at line 753.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer input drives frame/chunk metadata so blosc allocates a small destination chunk buffer, then zstd sequence decoding reaches the slow-path `ZSTD_execSequenceEnd` (near block end). With crafted sequence literal/match lengths that pass existing `sequenceLength <= oend-op` checks but execute safecopy near the end, the `oend_w` underflow/assumption mismatch allows an out-of-bounds write past the heap chunk. Data flow: fuzz_decompress_frame -> frame_decompress_chunk -> blosc_d/zstd_wrap_decompress -> ZSTD_decompressBlock_internal -> ZSTD_decompressSequences -> ZSTD_execSequenceEnd -> ZSTD_safecopy.
